critical_vulnerabilities_audited.title: Unbound Operation Type and Destination Node in QuorumMutationPermit
critical_vulnerabilities_audited.vulnerability_analysis: In Phase 4.4, QuorumPermitGrant binds epoch, commit_index, voter_id, request_id, object_id, shard_id, version, and payload_sha256_hex. However, it does not explicitly bind the destination target_node_id or the specific operation type (StageShard vs CommitManifest vs DeleteShard vs GarbageCollectShard). A valid permit intended for Node A could hypothetically be relayed to Node B storing the same shard identity, or a StageShard permit could be re-purposed for a destructive deletion operation.
critical_vulnerabilities_audited.architectural_remediation: Extend QuorumPermitGrant and QuorumMutationPermit to include PermitOperationType and target_node: NodeId, authenticating under domain tag FSP-PERMIT-GRANT-V2 while maintaining backwards compatibility for existing Phase 4.4 tests.

critical_vulnerabilities_audited.title: Control Plane Quorum Loss vs Data Durability Disconnect in 5-Host RS(20,12) Topology
critical_vulnerabilities_audited.vulnerability_analysis: Under a 5-host physical topology with 4 shards per host for RS(20,12), the loss of 2 physical hosts causes 8 shard failures. Since 12 shards survive (>= k=12), the payload data is 100% durable and mathematically reconstructable. However, if the metadata control plane uses a standard 3-voter quorum co-located on the first 3 hosts, losing hosts 1 and 2 destroys 2 out of 3 voters, causing metadata quorum loss. The control plane fails closed, preventing mutations and online reads, even though data durability is completely unharmed.
critical_vulnerabilities_audited.architectural_remediation: Formalize 5-voter metadata quorum (requiring 3 of 5 voters, surviving any 2 host losses simultaneously with RS(20,12) data durability) and implement an offline emergency read tool allowing direct data reconstruction from surviving storage nodes when the coordinator control plane is completely unavailable.

critical_vulnerabilities_audited.title: Erasure Coding Matrix Naming Discrepancy (Cauchy vs. Vandermonde)
critical_vulnerabilities_audited.vulnerability_analysis: Phase 4.4 documentation occasionally referenced Vandermonde submatrices, whereas the underlying engine in src/coding/reed_solomon.rs is systematically implemented using a Cauchy generator matrix C_{p,j} = 1 / (x_p ^ y_j) over GF(2^8). Standard Vandermonde matrices over GF(2^8) can have singular submatrices, whereas Cauchy matrices guarantee the MDS property for all submatrices. Codec interoperability must be rigorously validated and documented.
critical_vulnerabilities_audited.architectural_remediation: Audit and document the exact Systematic Cauchy Reed-Solomon generator matrix construction, confirm MDS invertibility for all submatrices, and establish cross-version differential tests.
